claims.text: The target material is a multi-principal-element refractory high-entropy alloy system.
The refractory alloy system has a vast compositional space.
Traditional thermo-kinetic and simulation methods have not optimized this refractory alloy composition space.
A machine-learning-assisted high-throughput screening method can rapidly identify intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-density RHEA compositions.
The proposed machine-learning model is trained using combined simulation and experimental datasets.
The model can predict optimal alloy compositions under realistic processing parameters.
High-throughput computational screening can rapidly explore large HEA composition spaces.
The screening can be conducted under processing conditions that mimic real-world RHEA fabrication.
Optimized elemental ratios determine phase stability, lattice distortion, and microstructural configuration.
The machine-learning model identifies nonlinear correlations among composition, lattice distortion, phase balance, and mechanical properties.
These learned correlations enable rapid screening of the RHEA composition space.
The screening can identify alloys that overcome the strength-ductility trade-off.
The screening can reduce alloy weight while improving strength and ductility.
The designed RHEAs will have higher intrinsic strength, greater ductility, and lower density than alloys designed through traditional methods.
Traditional thermo-kinetic analysis and brute-force simulation are too time-consuming to explore the HEA composition space efficiently.
Model predictions are reliable only within the composition and processing ranges represented by the training data.
Extrapolation beyond the represented training domain may produce uncertain predictions.
Biases in the training data could reduce prediction accuracy.
